The school has children at the heart of all its decisions, exemplified by the values of ‘my child is your child’- Ofsted November 2024
Welcome
Solin Flash - Headteacher
Pound Park Nursery School is a Maintained Nursery School in the heart of Charlton, within the Royal Borough of Greenwich.
Opened in 1944, we are an established Outstanding Nursery School delivering high quality early education to children aged 2-4 years. Our Nursery School really is an adventurous woodland oasis for young children to explore. Our highly qualified teachers and practitioners support, encourage and facilitate learning opportunities enabling our children to be confident and independent life long learners.

Vision
Pound Park Nursery School welcomes all children and families, offering high quality opportunities, support and care at all times. As a fully inclusive setting, we embrace the diverse community which we serve and celebrate the uniqueness of each child to give all our children the best possible start in life.
Through exciting, positive and stimulating activities, our passionate and qualified staff team provide a diverse, safe and caring environment. Children are motivated through play to connect with the outdoors and the world around them, to learn new skills and to become confident, independent and lifelong learners.
We value the partnerships that we have with our families and actively encourage their participation in their child's learning and developmental journey at Pound Park Nursery School.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pound Park Nursery School - Greenwich Community Schools Partnership
pageCache.text:
Greenwich Community Schools Partnership
Pound Park works collaboratively with several other schools within Greenwich across the education sector which include Nursery, Primary, Secondary and Special Schools. The aim and shared values of our schools is to support all of our families and children to enable youngsters to thrive and be successful learners. We support each other as established schools to drive school improvement and develop innovative approaches to education.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pound Park Nursery School - History of Pound Park
pageCache.text:
History of Pound Park
Pound Park Nursery School is a maintained nursery school run by the Royal Borough of Greenwich. Built in 1944, Pound Park was set up to cater for the children whose parents were involved in the war effort. Developed with a core value of delivering high quality early education and having qualified teachers, Pound Park continues this ethos until the present day. Pound Park established itself as a model of good practice for the education of children aged three and four years.
In 2004, Pound Park added the Up to Threes Unit as part of the Neighbourhood Nursery Initiative and we welcomed our first group of children aged 3 months to 3 years old. This service later converted to the Together for Twos programme to support vulnerable two year olds in the area.
In 2006 Pound Park, in conjunction with Sure Start Charlton, became a Children’s Centre and another new building- the family room- was added.
In 2011 Pound Park Children’s Centre federated with Cardwell Children’s Centre and in 2013 we federated with Mulgrave Children’s Centre. We ran services, in partnership with other core providers, for families and the community in Charlton and Woolwich.
In 2014, the Children’s Centres separated from the main nursery school and a school’s company (Central Greenwich Children’s Centres) was formed to manage the four federated children’s centres - Pound Park Children’s Centre, Cardwell Children’s Centre, Mulgrave Children’s Centre and Eglinton Children’s Centre.
Distinctly, and under the direction of the Governors and the Headteacher, Pound Park Nursery School and Together for Twos continues to be federated with the Together for Twos provision contained within Cardwell Children’s Centre. Together we offer a high quality provision for 2, 3 and 4 year old children. We maintain a strong relationship with the local Children’s Centres to enable our families to access a range of services.
In September 2015, we integrated our two year olds into the main nursery school at Pound Park. This means that our two, three and four year old children are able to learn from each other in an outstanding provision together.

Partnerships
Here at Pound Park we believe in the quality work we can do to benefit our children through working collaboratively with other schools and organisations. To find our more about some of the partnerships we are part of follow the links:-

pageCache.pageTitle: Pound Park Nursery School - EYFS Curriculum
pageCache.text:
EYFS Curriculum
At Pound Park Nursery School we are concerned that the children should enjoy coming to school, feel successful and know they are in a happy secure environment where they are able to work towards their full potential.
The following statements indicate how we feel that children learn best:
Curriculum Statement
The school provides a curriculum which is especially suited to the needs of young children and covers all the areas of learning described in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS).
Prime Areas
Personal and social and emotional development - which focuses on children learning how to manage their feelings and behaviour as well as build relationships and develop confidence.
Physical development - which focuses on children developing physical control, mobility, awareness of space and manipulative skills in the indoor and outdoor enviroment. This also includes Health and Self-Care.
Communication and language development - which focuses on children developing competence in speaking, listening, attention and understanding.
Specific Areas
Literacy - which focuses on children's first steps towards becoming readers and writers.
Mathematics - which focuses on children's first steps in exploring number, shape, space and measure; as well as problem solving
Understanding the world - which focuses on children's developing knowledge and understanding of their environment, other people and features of the natural and made world as well as technology.
Expressive arts and design - which focuses on the development of the children's imagination and their ability to communicate and express ideas and feelings in a creative way.
We plan daily as a whole school for the indoors and outside. This is largely based on the children's interests, rhythms of the year and significant events and experiences. At Pound Park the areas of the curriculum are shared across the four classrooms. Our 2 year olds and 3 year olds are integrated into the main nursery school and free flow across the four classrooms and garden.
You can find out more about the early years foundation stage via the following websites:
http://www.foundationyears.org.uk/
https://www.gov.uk/early-years-foundation-stage

pageCache.pageTitle: Pound Park Nursery School - Enrichment Activities at Pound Park
pageCache.text:
Enrichment Activities at Pound Park
Interactive Music Making
We have a trained Interactive Music teacher who runs sessions on a weekly basis to engage children and extend their learning through music. The sessions support children’s understanding with particular focus on listening and attention. Children develop their music skills and abilities to play instruments all through having lots of fun.
Forest School
Stated as a ‘Forest School Centre of Excellence’ by Ofsted in 2015, Pound Park delivers an integrated outdoor education throughout daily provision. We have three forest school leaders who work with parent volunteers to support children’s learning in the outdoors. Not only do we have a small woodland space on site we also have a large space within Gilberts Pit. Children learn new skills through wildlife hunts, plant and tree identification as well as whittling, sawing and lighting camp fires to cook on. By engaging and training children in risky activities in the outdoors, children develop sophisticated skills in being able to manage safety and learn skills they may not pick up anywhere else. Forest school has school a significant positive impact on children’s language, their ability to make relationships and understand the world around them.
Yoga
Yoga develops body and mind.
At Pound Park we guide the children through a series of moves and poses in a healthy, non-competitive environment. Providing yoga lessons at Pound Park, we are offer a alternative way to handle challenges in the classroom. To engage children we teach Yoga through fun and play- we use books, props and sensory experiences.

Governors
Our Parent and Staff Governors are elected. The Headteacher has a standing post, co-opted governors are nominated and approved by the Governing Body for a term which lasts 4 years at a time. All Governors have signed a Register of Interests to indicate whether they have a potential conflict of interest and there are none other than as recorded.
If you are interested in becoming a governor please let us know.
The full governing body meets each term. There are two committees that also meet termly - Learning and Achievement and Resources Committees.

SEN Information Report (Local Offer)
All Greenwich maintained schools have a similar approach to meeting the needs of pupils with Special Educational Needs and/or disabilities (SEND), and are supported by the Local Authority to ensure that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs, make the best possible progress in school. All schools are supported to be as inclusive as possible, with the needs of pupils with a Special Educational Need(s) and/or disability being met in a mainstream setting wherever possible, where families want this to happen.

Children's Speech and Language Therapy Service (Oxleas)
Greenwich Children's Speech and Language Therapy Service has an open access policy for children under 5 which includes self referral via drop in assessment and clinic sessions.

Special Education Needs and Disability Information, Advice and Support Service (SENDIASS)
This free service is available to parents, children and young people living in the Royal Borough of Greenwich.
They can help by providing access to impartial and confidential guidance and support on matters relating to Special Educational Needs and Disabilities, including education, schools, national and local policy and practice, statutory assessment and Education, Health and Care plans.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pound Park Nursery School - Early Communication Together
pageCache.text:
Early Communication Together Team
Admissions/Referrals
Referrals are provided for children who have completed an initial block of therapy with the Oxleas Early Years Speech and Language Therapy Service. This is the only pathway for referrals.
What is the purpose of the 6 Week Hub?
To understand how their child communicates.
To communicate what I need or want
To build attention and understanding skills
To manage transitions between activities with support
What do the Hubs look like for me and my child?
Families are supported to help their child’s skills using key strategies such as:
Imitating their child’s sound, words and actions
Following their child’s interests in play
Interpreting their child’s attempts at communication
Introducing more fun to their child's play
Any other relevant strategies
What happens when my 6 week hub is finished?
Once the six-week programme is completed, the ECT team will do an outreach visit once a term to the child's setting to work with the staff to support the child's needs. Please see the ECT Policy below for more information.
ECT Policy and FAQs
ECT Policy FAQs
What other support can I access with ECT?
The Early Communication Together Team run weekly Stay and Play sessions (term time only) at Pound Park Nursery School, 1 - 2.30pm.
You do not need to book, you are welcome to drop in.

SEND
At Pound Park Nursery School we aim to create a listening atmosphere and environment where everyone is welcomed, all individual needs are met, support is given and information shared.
We aim to enable all children to become confident learners with a growing ability to communicate their own views.
We are committed to working in partnership with parents/carers and outside agencies to raise aspirations and expectations for children with SEND by focusing on the whole child to ensure positive outcomes and to enable all children to fulfil their potential.
All policies can be found on our Policies page
Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator Mira Harder can be contacted by email on senco@poundpark.greenwich.sch.uk or via the school office.
If you are unhappy with the support or arrangements in place for your child regarding their Special Educational Needs and Disabilities, in the first instance please speak to you child's Key Person and the Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator.
If you are still unhappy then please refer to our complaints policy.
